parser_contract.instruction_definition: Every cuobjdump offset-bearing instruction, including predicate-false UIADD3, NOP padding and terminal self-BRA. Encoding-only lines excluded. Counts are static and do not equal executed instructions or performance.

scoreboard_decode.interpretation: Static encoded scheduling dependencies; not measured runtime stalls or fully hidden latency.

source_M1_contract.cast_DAG: Each final S1..S4 and T1..T4 is cast once from its FP32 dependency value to input precision with RN; dependencies never consume an earlier rounded S/T. Original quadrants remain original rounded lowp.
source_M1_contract.P_order: P1 through P7 per K16; each native FP32 P accumulator retains contributions across all K16 stages. No stage-local C contribution M2 schedule.
source_M1_contract.output: Only C(v0,v1) top physical rows are emitted. C row=lane/4+8*(v/2), col=2*(lane%4)+(v%2). Four quadrants each store one adjacent float2 per lane; v2/v3 discarded.
source_M1_contract.identity: Fast path alpha==1, beta==±0. Kernel has no C0 argument and emits U directly, preserving signed-zero bits. Dynamic coefficients use per-call planner fallback.
source_M1_contract.guard: Row-major FP16/BF16; positive M/N/K<=32768 and multiples32; lda>=K, ldb/ldd>=N; lda/ldb multiples8, ldd even; conservative int64 address span guard; A/B16-byte aligned and D8-byte aligned. Unused C0/ldc ignored for beta0.
source_M1_contract.stream_and_allocation: Static shared, caller stream, no run allocation or host synchronization. Lower A rows zero once, full-warp publish barrier, stage fills top rows/B, full-warp publish barrier, synchronous seven MMAs, reuse barrier.
source_M1_contract.fallback: Formal plan.cpp checks each runtime binding and dispatches19->16->15->14->12->packed7; unsupported or insufficient A/B alignment can select Dense through common dispatch. Constructor creates supported route resources; helper19 alone throws on incompatible use.
source_M1_contract.overflow: Owner/grid counters fit int (maximum parent32768; grid2048x2048), all global stride multiplication retains int64 Problem strides.
source_M1_contract.discarded_bottom_finite_caution: No claim that all discarded native C slots stay finite: finite original inputs may overflow final lowp transforms; zero-bottom times infinite B can form discarded NaN. Native output rows are independent and bottom rows are never emitted.

resource_comparison.shared_accounting: Source and CUPTI staticSharedMemory=5376; cuobjdump resource SHARED=6400 for both16/19. Additional1024 compiled reserve origin unverified; do not silently equate these fields.
resource_comparison.spills: Both selected variants/dtypes report STACK0 LOCAL0 and have no LDL/STL opcodes. Profiler localMemoryPerThread0; its separate raw localMemoryTotal is retained without inferring spills.
resource_comparison.aggregate_work: Relative to16x8 owners, 8x8 halves logical M ownership and doubles CTA count. Each CTA still issues7 full native16x8 HMMA per K16, so aggregate native HMMA and logical B raw loads/transform work double. A raw loads per CTA halve, approximately preserving aggregate A raw traffic; source lower A zero prologue is additional. Output vector stores per CTA halve, preserving aggregate emitted output. This is not a reduction in total matrix arithmetic or total B work.
resource_comparison.aggregate_static_transform_cost: Both dtype:16 has48 transform FADD plus28 final U FADD;19 has32 transform FADD plus14 final U FADD. Doubled CTA count means64 vs48 aggregate transform FADD per corresponding output area, while final U work stays28. These are static instruction counts with a defined source stage, not measured dynamic throughput.
resource_comparison.cache_comparison: 16 and19 both use plain LDG.E raw loads without .CONSTANT;19 all64-bit versus16 mixed128/64-bit. Identity15 used .CONSTANT, so comparisons with15 also change cache policy.
resource_comparison.schedule: 19:7 next raw LDGs precede first HMMA; final8th LDG follows first HMMA and4LDSM, then precedes remaining6HMMA. First next load precedes all LDSM. No reference to next raw destination registers occurs before backedge; first next iteration STS waits barrier5/0x20.16:all8 next raw LDGs precede first HMMA but5LDSM already issued. Both expose static overlap, without proving fully hidden latency.
resource_comparison.last_iteration: All19 next LDGs share @!P2; P2 compares kh<=stage counter. Source next_k<kh, all1024 allowedK CPU proof, and short K32/64/96 GPU/SAN cases jointly support no final extra read. Static opcode count alone cannot prove this.

aggregate_raw_input_bytes_per_correspond.meaning: Logical original-lowp loads; not measured DRAM bytes or cache miss traffic. A remains2048 bytes per corresponding area, B increases1024->2048 bytes.

limitations: Audit executed no GPU, build, benchmark or git; only this authorized evidence JSON is published.
Parent-provided source commit is recorded separately from observed exact source/test/binary hashes.
Static resource/order/scoreboard analysis does not establish achieved occupancy, bandwidth, stall hiding, causality, or a physical speed floor.
Native19 bitwise coverage applies only to shapes/coefficients that satisfy strict19 guard; other19 requests can exercise fallback.
Exact finite integer, owner-label and dyadic checks are structural/bitwise evidence, separate from mixed precision certification.
Single Nsight samples are not steady-state latency distributions; cache form, owner geometry, raw width and SIMD transformation changes prevent single-factor performance attribution.
CPU geometry proofs include a narrow-N48 shape rejected by native19 guard; this verifies index geometry, not native route support.
Racecheck/synccheck coverage is all-candidate smoke; short-K owner19, Graph19, rebind and M1 bitwise records are present in full correctness/memcheck rather than those two smoke logs.
Strict930 refers to31 requested configurations, not31 distinct actual implementations; six of thirty owner19 trials use Dense upper-range fallback.
